STEP 1 - Vessel type: The food sits on a white dish with a rim band and curved inner walls rising on all sides, with the food mound well inside. This is a shallow bowl (or deep-ish serving dish). Choose: shallow bowl.

STEP 2 - Vessel size:
a) Type: a square-ish white serving bowl/plate is typically 20-25 cm.
b) Reference: the strawberry halves are about 3-4 cm across and blueberries about 1.5 cm. The dish spans roughly 6-7 strawberry widths across its inner area (about 22-24 cm of visible rim), consistent with a ~23 cm width.
Final width: 23 cm.

STEP 3 - Food items:
- Blueberries: the surface holds roughly 70-80 visible berries. Counting hidden berries underneath (pile about 2 deep), estimate ~150 berries. Blueberry weight ~1.5 g each → 150 × 1.5 ≈ 225 g. Using the bowl-volume method as a check: capacity = 0.2 × 23³ / 1000 ≈ 2.4 L (shallow); fill ~0.3 of the mound volume in the centre → ~0.3 L of fruit at 0.6 g/ml ≈ 180 g total fruit. Blueberries take roughly 60% of that: ~110-200 g. Take ~150 g.
- Strawberries: about 6-7 halves/pieces visible, each roughly 20-25 g → ~140 g total, with a few hidden pieces, take ~150 g.

Thickness check: the food mound peaks about 2-3 cm above the base, averaging ~1.5 cm, consistent with the fill estimate above.

STEP 4 - Hidden food: no base layer (no rice or grains) is visible; the fruit sits directly on the dish, so no extra items.

STEP 5 - kcal per 100 g:
- Blueberries: 57 kcal/100 g
- Strawberries: 32 kcal/100 g

Totals: blueberries ~150 g → ~86 kcal; strawberries ~150 g → ~48 kcal. Total food ≈ 300 g, ≈ 134 kcal.
